messages:
Alex: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a "tiered-penalty + grace-credit" enforcement interface for abuse throttling. Need alignment on: enforcement location (edge vs central), telemetry contract, and how cross-region credit sync should work.
Maria: Can you sketch a short request flow example? I want to see where credits are consumed vs when penalties apply. :thinking:
Alex: Sure. Example: incoming req -> edge admission checks local grace credits -> if exceeded, consult central penalty service via xrpc -> central issues penalty token (short TTL) -> edge enforces. Grace credits are deducted locally first.
Jamal: Concern: that xrpc call adds tail latency and a new availability surface. If central is slow we end up increasing 429s. How do we avoid coupling to central for steady-state?
Sasha: We should make central only for stateful decisions (new abuse detection/score) and allow local fallback rules. Local decisions should be authoritative for fast-path. Central can asynchronously reconcile.
Ethan: Agree with Sasha. Also: telemetry must capture both local-decisions and central overrides. We need a single trace id per request so we can attribute token usage vs penalty reasons.
Maria: What about fairness? If local grace credits are per-edge, tenants with traffic concentrated in one region could get more benefit. Do we shard credits by tenant+region or keep global credits with a probabilistic soft-lease?
Alex: Proposal A: region-scoped grace buckets + periodic central rebalance (every 10s). Proposal B: global logical credits with probabilistic admission at edge (sampled token exchange). A gives stability, B gives stronger global fairness but more central load.
Jamal: Option B sounds like it could overload the central broker under bursty abuse. Maybe we need hybrid: local fast-path plus a global soft-budget that triggers stricter penalties when central signals scarcity.
Sasha: Hybrid sounds reasonable. Implementation detail: represent credits as 64-bit counters with monotonic increments and use delta sync to central. Avoid per-request full state fetch.
Ethan: Can we leverage the existing credit-service APIs? We already have an endpoint that accepts "delta" and returns a small response with new horizon. Keep payload tiny: `{delta: 10, tenant: "t123"}`.
Alex: Good call. We'll reuse credit-service delta API. Telemetry contract (proposal): every admission decision emits: `trace_id, tenant, edge_id, local_cr, central_cr, decision, penalty_code`. Also emit metrics: local_grace_remaining (gauge), central_latency_ms (histogram).
Maria: Also need an ops playbook: if central is unreachable for >30s, edges should move to conservative mode: halve grace buckets and tighten thresholds. Document expected customer-visible behavior.
Jamal: One more: token accounting for streaming completions. We charge tokens after generation; but admission happens before. Need a refund/charge reconciliation flow if we pre-admit tokens but the request is short.
Sasha: Plan: edges pre-authorize up to an expected max per-request, then reconcile on completion with actual usage. Reconciliation writes a negative delta when usage < preauth. Keep reconciliation idempotent.
Ethan: Reconciliation must be robust to duplicate callbacks. Use idempotency keys (request_id) and the credit-service should dedupe.
ops-bot: integration-tests/penalty-probe ran: 12/15 passing. Failures are timeouts in central-penalty-simulator. Logs: `xrpc timeout to penalty-service 504`.
Alex: Thanks. For the RFC follow-up: action items: (1) add hybrid design section (edge fast-path + central soft-budget) (2) define telemetry fields and dashboards (3) ops playbook for central outage (4) implement idempotent delta API usage for preauth/reconcile.
Maria: +1 on action items. Can we add a short table of latency budget impacts to doc? Need to quantify 50th/95th p99 delta if central check is required.
Alex: Will add. Tentative timeline: prototype in edge proxy for preauth/reconcile this sprint, central soft-budget in next.
Jamal: I'll volunteer to run chaos tests for central outages once we have prototype.
Sasha: I'll draft the telemetry schema and a sample dashboard.
Ethan: I'll wire idempotency keys into the SDK and make the client retry-safe.
Maria: :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks, everyone — I'll update the RFC and ping when PR is up.
